title: Mint Chutney (Pudina Chutney)

ingredients.title: For the Chutney
items: Fresh mint leaves – 1 tightly packed cup, washed and stems mostly removed
Fresh coriander leaves – 1 tightly packed cup, washed, tender stems included
Fresh ginger – 1 tsp, peeled and roughly chopped
Salt – ½ tsp, or to taste
Cold water – 2–3 tbsp, or as needed

instruction.title: Prepare the Herbs
steps: Pick the tender mint leaves and rinse thoroughly in cold water to remove any grit.
Pat the mint leaves gently dry.
Wash the coriander leaves, keeping the tender stems and trimming away thick ends.
Pat the coriander dry before blending.

instruction.title: Blend the Ingredients
steps: Add mint leaves, coriander leaves, green chilies, ginger, and garlic if using to a high-speed blender.
Add lemon juice, roasted cumin powder, black salt, regular salt, and sugar.
Add 1–2 tbsp cold water to help the ingredients blend smoothly.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.

instruction.title: Adjust the Consistency
steps: Add a little more cold water if a thinner chutney is desired.
Blend briefly again until the desired consistency is reached.

instruction.title: Taste & Balance
steps: Taste the chutney and adjust the salt, lemon juice, or green chili as needed.
If the mint tastes slightly bitter, add a small pinch of sugar to balance it.
The finished chutney should have fresh mint flavor, citrus tang, moderate heat, and a subtle earthy cumin note.

instruction.title: Serve & Store
steps: Serve immediately with samosas, pakoras, kebabs, sandwiches, or as a spread.
Transfer leftovers to an airtight glass or food-grade plastic container.
For longer storage, freeze the chutney in ice cube trays.

chefTips: Herbs: Use tender mint leaves and avoid old, thick stems for a smoother chutney and cleaner flavor.
Color: Use cold water or a small ice cube while blending to reduce heat from the blender and help maintain the bright green color.
Balance: Lemon provides acidity, sugar balances mint bitterness, and roasted cumin adds earthy depth.
Creamy variation: For chaat or street-food applications, mix the chutney with an equal amount of yogurt for a milder, creamier dip.
Storage: Avoid reactive metal containers; glass or food-grade plastic is preferable for storing fresh chutney.
